title: Retire Graph/Graphify from active EQCOFE project workflow
description: Owner-directed retirement of the repository-integrated Graph/Graphify layer. Remove tracked Graphify skills, hooks, health/watch/refresh tooling and graph-specific active governance contracts; remove graph-first requirements from agent instructions and local Codex startup; reconcile live Current State/Master Roadmap so Graph is no longer a gate, dependency or evidence requirement. Preserve completed historical step records as history only. No runtime application, API/OpenAPI, database, dependency, CI workflow, branch protection or product behavior change.

evidence.owner_policy: Graph/Graphify is no longer part of active EQCOFE governance. Future graphing, if explicitly requested, is optional whole-project analysis only and cannot block project execution.

acceptance_criteria.description: All tracked operational Graphify skills, hooks, refresh/watch/health/state tooling and graph-specific operational documentation are removed.
AGENTS.md and the local Codex launcher contain no graph-first, freshness, watch, refresh or Graphify dependency.
acceptance_criteria.verification: exact text search and launcher review

acceptance_criteria.description: The four graph-specific Task Contracts are removed and generated Task Catalog is exactly reconciled, while completed historical task/step records are not rewritten as if Graphify never existed.
acceptance_criteria.verification: task catalog exactness and history review

acceptance_criteria.description: Current State and Master Roadmap record Step 63 as canonically closed, Step 64 as active, and Graph/Graphify as retired/non-blocking.

acceptance_criteria.verification: diff scope review and canonical CI

acceptance_criteria.description: Local graph artifacts are not part of the repository and the Owner receives a one-line local cleanup command for existing graphify-out/worktree artifacts.

external_gate_evidence.rule: MEDIUM-risk developer-tooling/governance retirement. Human Gate not required because this task directly executes the Owner's explicit removal directive.
